notes: Actual results for calendar year 2024, as the county reported them to the Minnesota Office of the State Auditor. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.

Governmental funds are reported by function. Enterprise funds (water, sewer, electric, liquor stores and others) count their operating revenue and expenses with depreciation left out and capital outlay counted when paid, plus debt payments.
Borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
General government, housing and redevelopment, economic development and conservation of natural resources count as overhead.
Debt is bonds, other long-term debt and short-term debt outstanding at year end, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Minnesota county candidates file campaign finance reports with their county auditor, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Minnesota yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
